summary.title: What every computer science major should know
summary.one_liner: A curriculum-style checklist of the skills, languages, and reading a computer science major should pick up, from portfolios and Unix to theory, security, and parallelism.
takeaways: Build a public code portfolio (blog, per-project pages, hosted repositories) because it shows ability better than a resume or GPA.
Learn a core set of practical skills: fluent Unix/command line, Linux administration, LaTeX and presentation tools, and git or svn version control.
Study a broad range of languages and paradigms (Racket, C, Standard ML, Haskell, Prolog, and others) and implement at least an interpreter.
Cover the theory and foundations: discrete math, data structures and algorithms, models of computation, complexity (P vs NP), architecture, and operating systems.
Treat security, cryptography, testing, and user experience as core topics rather than optional extras.
summary.summary: This is an opinionated essay by Matt Might listing what he thinks every computer science major should know. It is organized as sections, each covering a topic such as portfolios, Unix philosophy, systems administration, programming languages, discrete math, theory, architecture, networking, security, cryptography, and parallelism. Each section gives specific recommendations (for example, projects to build or tasks to solve) and a short reading list. The page is a set of recommendations rather than a tutorial, so readers get a curriculum outline and pointers to books.
